item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I was told this was where stuff started to get good (not counting the Prologue) and it's true. The characterization is getting really compelling.

Overall it could stand to be edited down, but still.

Nitpicks:

“Hurting more.” Mary-Ann’s voice was almost a whisper.

This… doesn't work at all for me. :/ The sentiment is undercut by the cliche and the on-the-nose-ness. Honestly, that could be much more effective if that line was completely cut, or if she got evasive at the last sec and says "You know" or something like that, and he still nods and the conversation continues as before.

“Yeah. Pretty good for sticking a post-it note with ‘Abraham was a pretty rad dude’ on the wall.”

Pretty awesome line.

A chuckle rose from that. A sad one, but at least it existed.

Eh… and we're back in the doldrums again. There's no need to be this on the nose.

Also, in this section, it starts getting more confusing who's talking. Dialogue tags could be better paired with the lines being spoken.

“Very well then. My greatest fear is myself.”

Man, see… this line deserves to be cut. It would be much more effective if he just launched into the story he's gonna tell. The reader will get it, I promise. I mean, the other lines after make it blisteringly clear (and they're much better lines).

In here,” He pointed to his head.

Typo — that shouldn't be a comma. Should be ellipses or a period. Not sure which, so I didn't fix it.

Another sad chuckle.

This one's more nitpicky but I don't think you need 'sad' here. That's not trusting the characters and dialogue to get that across. And they're working really well, so that's a shame. (Actually, pretty much most of my critique above here is about 'not trusting your material'.)

Man… the voice quavering and sniffling stuff too… same deal.

The promise section of dialogue is pretty meh — it would honestly get the same idea across if he just let her know that he knew she'd endure, and gave her the gift. The gift bit is good regardless. It should have more lines edited out too, but it works.

EDIT: You also don't need the song lyrics. Not a big deal though.

Overall, this is definitely good. +1

EDIT: Much improved with the new minor edits. (Not that I didn't already like it, of course.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is thick with in-jokes and references to jokes, both from the wiki and general culture. But you've managed to work them all in subtly and organically so that none of them seem like jokes, but rather just things that exist for the characters.

It reads like a real moment between real people, who just happen to live in a world that we consider fantastical and somewhere on the scale from amusing to horrific. Masterfully done, and one of the few times I honestly wish I could up-vote twice.

item.title: Re: LETS MAKE CHECKLIST
item.content:encoded:
Fun commentary fact: I was considering using "Amarillo" for the song at the end, because it really is the perfect song for Mary-Ann. (For those of you reading who don't know it, just listen to those lyrics) "Demon Days" won out though, as it fit the mood of the moment better.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Not sure if joking or serious, so I'll address both.

If joking: The party for the Australian Church of Australia was held elsewhere, because there was not enough room to store the beer and the fisticuffs ring. Also the Australian Church of Australia is now definitely a thing in this universe.

If serious: The year before, people ended up in the hospital because arguments over Jesus' divinity broke out before dinner even started. We are dealing with a group made up of factions who have been fighting with each other since their inception: getting them to agree on where to go to lunch is a difficulty. You can guarantee that there's a good chunk of Initiative leadership that frowns on these sort of parties just because of prior fiascoes and the trouble they cause.

As Mary-Ann commented, the name was tongue in cheek, and you can guarantee that everyone else was in on it. You can kinda tell with the "(Check Your Attitude and Weapons at the Door)" part. Or the part where the name is completely and totally overwrought to the point of ridiculousness.
